text:
sam (secops): Noticed increased tls handshake failures between apac-ingest and eu-proxy starting ~09:10Z after the keystore IAM policy rollout. KMS returns AccessDenied on Unwrap calls. :warning:

leah (infra): Can you paste the failing log lines?

sam (secops): Sure, from eu-proxy-3: 
```
2026-04-05T09:12:03Z proxy[pid=210]: tls: handshake error from 10.12.4.8: remote error: tls: bad certificate
2026-04-05T09:12:04Z proxy[pid=210]: kms: decrypt error: AccessDenied: caller is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on resource projects/redwood/keystores/primary
```

omar (eng-sre): I see the same span across multiple nodes. The keystore policy applied in infra-cd dropped the previous binding for serviceAccount:cert-rotator@redwood.iam by mistake (policy diff had remove-only chunk).

rita (platform): Was that an intentional scope reduction? We had an approved change to tighten keystore roles but infra-cd config didn't include rotator in the new list.

leah (infra): It was meant to remove legacy roles, but rotator binding was still referenced in a separate overlay. Looks like a merge conflict got resolved silently by the pipeline.

oncall: Immediate mitigation options: 1) re-add the binding to keystore policy, 2) restart rotator pods in affected regions to pick up permissions, 3) temporarily add a short grace window on proxies to accept cached TLS sessions for an extra 45s.

sam (secops): Do the policy re-add and restart. Also enable KMS UnwrapDenied alert to trigger before client-facing errors exceed threshold.

leah (infra): Applying quick fix now. Running: 
```bash
# reapply binding
cloudkms keystore add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood/keystores/primary \
  --member=serviceAccount:cert-rotator@redwood.iam --role=roles/keystore.reader
# rollout restart rotator in apac/eu
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/cert-rotator-apac
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/cert-rotator-eu
```

omar (eng-sre): Rolling back traffic automation to fallback pools while this heals. Observability: 5xx spike correlates with policy apply window.

audit-bot: ERROR: 2026-04-05T09:11:48Z - policy.apply by infra-cd removed iamBinding for cert-rotator@redwood.iam on projects/redwood/keystores/primary (no MR metadata attached).

rita (platform): That's an audit/control gap. The change came from infra-cd with no attached MR id; we need to enforce a policy that infra-cd only applies keystore policy diffs if an MR tag is present and signed-off.

sam (secops): I'm opening a vuln-triage ticket: "keystore IAM drift without audit trail" and assigning to platform+infra. Suggested mitigations: enforce infra-cd policy attachment, CI check for keystore-dependent services coverage, and a mandatory post-change validation that rotator SA retains required bindings.

leah (infra): Fix applied, rotator pods restarted. I see successful unwraps in the logs and TLS handshakes recovering. Monitoring will watch for 10 minutes then we can remove fallback routes.

omar (eng-sre): Can we add an automated verification step in the rollout pipeline that runs a certificate rotation dry-run and checks KMS unwrap success prior to promoting policy?

rita (platform): Yes — we'll add a gating job that simulates rotator access and queries keystore IAM bindings. Also adding alerting: UnwrapDenied rate > 1% triggers paging.

oncall: Marking incident mitigated for now. Please file a short postmortem with owners for: 1) infra-cd MR enforcement, 2) CI keystore coverage check, 3) proxy session-grace parameter, 4) KMS unwrap alerting, 5) audit-log backfill for the removed binding.

sam (secops): Postmortem created and initial action items assigned. Thanks for the quick response. :thumbsup:
